title: Google Unveils Gemini Agent for Work as Enterprise AI Race Heats Up
excerpt: At its "Gemini at Work 2026" event, Google Cloud introduced a single AI agent that works inside Workspace, Microsoft 365 and Slack, routing each task to the best model — Google's Gemini or Anthropic's Claude.
body:
• Google Cloud on October 8 unveiled the "Gemini agent," a single AI agent for work that plans tasks, uses tools, and plugs into a company's business systems to deliver finished work.
  • The agent works inside Google Workspace (Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Calendar, Drive, Slides, Chat), as well as Microsoft 365 and Slack, and connects to developer tools such as Git and Jira.
  • It routes each task to the best model — currently Google's Gemini and Anthropic's Claude — and lets companies create "coworker agents" with their own email addresses and scoped access.
  • What this means for you: if your team lives in Workspace, routine grunt work — drafting documents, answering routine emails, crunching spreadsheets, writing code — could move inside the tools you already use, with less switching between apps. Pricing and a consumer release were not disclosed.

Google Cloud on Thursday introduced the "Gemini agent," a single AI agent built for work, at its "Gemini at Work 2026" event, marking Google's biggest enterprise push yet in the race to put autonomous agents inside the office.

The agent is designed to function less like a chatbot and more like a colleague. It answers questions, handles tasks, creates content, and writes code. It plans the work, uses tools, connects to a company's business systems, and returns finished output in documents, email, and developer environments, Reuters reported.

Distribution is the bet. The agent works directly inside Google Workspace apps — Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Calendar, Drive, Slides, and Chat — and extends beyond them through Microsoft 365 and Slack. It also connects to development tools including Git and Jira, and carries data and analytics skills aimed at both technical teams and everyday users.

Context & Background

The launch lands in a crowded autumn for agentic AI. OpenAI introduced always-on agents called "Dots" on September 29 — one Dot per user, running on its GPT-6 Astra model inside ChatGPT, Slack, and Teams, initially for ChatGPT Pro subscribers. Meta launched its consumer personal AI agent "Muse," powered by Muse Spark 1.3, on September 8; analyst coverage from Citi put Muse at 6.6 million downloads and 1.8 million daily active users. xAI's Grok Bot has been in beta since August.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=O46sS3H5oMA

Google's answer is deliberately enterprise-first. Sundar Pichai, chief executive of Google and Alphabet, said the company is starting with business customers before rolling the agent out to consumers, with the aim of solving what he called the "harder problems around security, scale, and performance." Alphabet shares rose marginally on the announcement.

Impact & Analysis

"harder problems around security, scale, and performance."

— Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet

The enterprise-first sequencing is the substantive differentiator. Consumer agents live or die on virality; enterprise agents live or die on governance. By leading with security and scale, Google is pitching IT departments and CIOs — the buyers who actually control Workspace contracts — rather than chasing Meta's download numbers.

The model-routing design is equally notable. Instead of forcing every task through Gemini, the agent picks the best model for the job — currently Google's Gemini models and Anthropic's Claude models, with more to be added. The inclusion of a direct competitor's models is a concession that no single model wins every task, and a practical one: customers get Claude's strengths without a separate procurement.

The "coworker agents" feature goes further. Companies can create agents that act as team members, each with its own email address and access restricted to only the information it is given. Industry editions for financial services and legal work are in preview, with government, healthcare, and retail versions coming — a signal Google is targeting regulated sectors where auditability and data boundaries are the purchase criteria.

Diaspora Angle

The agent race matters directly for Indian IT services professionals and the global capability centers they staff: whoever wins the enterprise agent layer will set the workflow standards — and the reskilling agenda — for the millions of engineers and analysts whose daily work runs inside Workspace and Slack. India's deep-tech ambitions, from the IndiaAI mission to its services giants' own agent platforms, now have a new benchmark to clear.

What's Next

Google has not disclosed pricing, availability timelines, or when the agent reaches consumers — the gaps every enterprise buyer and rival will scrutinize first. The preview editions for financial services and legal are the near-term test of whether coworker agents survive contact with real compliance departments. Government and healthcare editions, where Google competes head-on with Microsoft's entrenched position, come later. The Deep View noted that Google's moat may be its distribution inside Workspace itself; the next question is whether customers grant an agent the same trust — and access — they grant an employee.
